name: Biafra
summary: Red, black and green horizontal bands with a golden half-sun of eleven rays in the black band. It was the flag of the Republic of Biafra, the secessionist state in south-eastern Nigeria during the Nigerian Civil War of 1967–1970.
origin: The Eastern Region of Nigeria declared independence as the Republic of Biafra on 30 May 1967, under Lieutenant Colonel Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu. The flag used the Pan-African red, black and green associated with Marcus Garvey's movement.

Biafra was defeated in January 1970 after a war and blockade in which an estimated one to three million people died, many from famine. The flag remains a symbol of Igbo identity and of Biafran separatist movements today.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those massacred in Northern Nigeria in 1966 and of those who died in the war.

symbols.name: Rising sun
symbols.description: A golden half-sun with eleven rays.
symbols.meaning: A glorious future; the eleven rays represent the eleven provinces of Biafra.

facts: The rising sun also appears on Biafra's coat of arms and currency.
Malawi's flag, adopted in 1964, also has a red rising sun in a black band of a red-black-green tricolour.
Biafra was recognised by only five UN member states: Tanzania, Gabon, Ivory Coast, Zambia and Haiti.
clues: Red, black and green bands with a golden half-sun in the black band.
Its sun's eleven rays stood for eleven provinces.
The flag of a secessionist state in West Africa in 1967–1970.
A landlocked country in south-east Africa has a similar flag with a red sun.
